recommended_next_phase: 149O.20L.7O.2D.1 -- HATP Principal/Signer Enrollment Contract Independent Verification. Must independently attack principal semantics (HPSE-REQ-001..008, including the disclosed PrincipalRecord.revoked_at schema gap), signer semantics (HPSE-REQ-009..017), provider profile (HPSE-REQ-018..020), authority_scope vocabulary (HBDC-REQ-071..076), registry schema (HPSE-REQ-021..025), the enrollment writer's API/preview/atomicity/locking design (HPSE-REQ-026..033, including the shared-lock finding), error vocabulary (HPSE-REQ-034), fail-closed behavior (HPSE-REQ-035..037), audit ordering (HPSE-REQ-038..039), enrollment authority separation (HPSE-REQ-040..041), election/CHGR requirements (HPSE-REQ-042..043), the hardware-credential prerequisite (HPSE-REQ-044..046), the named-but-unbuilt DeploymentBinding producer amendments (HPSE-REQ-047..048), the disclosed revocation-cascading gap (HPSE-REQ-049..050), runtime-provider separation (HPSE-REQ-051), timestamp grammar (HPSE-REQ-052), and both contracts' HMIC/HBDC-REQ-042 consequences. Must not implement anything; only after clean independent verification should implementation planning/building begin.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2D -- HATP Principal/Signer Enrollment Contract Architecture. FINAL VERDICT: HATP PRINCIPAL/SIGNER ENROLLMENT CONTRACT ARCHITECTURE READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. Contract-text/architecture-only phase; zero Dell mutation (zero commands issued, read or write), zero production .py bytes modified. Froze two artifacts. (1) A new companion contract, docs/contracts/HATP_PRINCIPAL_SIGNER_ENROLLMENT_CONTRACT.md (HPSE-001 v1.0, 52 requirements HPSE-REQ-001..052, mechanically verified sequential/no-gaps/no-duplicates), formalizing HATP-REQ-036/037's conceptual enrollment procedure into concrete requirements for a Principal/Signer enrollment writer -- reusing hatp_bootstrap.py's already-existing PrincipalRecord/SignerRecord schema unchanged, and every atomicity/locking/audit-ordering/error-vocabulary/preview idiom hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py already establishes, rather than inventing parallel ones. (2) A narrow amendment to docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md, v1.1 to v1.2 (new Section 16.2, HBDC-REQ-071..076, CBD-11), freezing DeploymentBinding.authority_scope to a single-member closed vocabulary, CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT -- selected because zero real consumers in this codebase (traced directly in human_approval_trusted_provenance.py) ever read authority_scope's content, only its record's .status. Key freshly-derived findings, independently re-traced from primary source this session, not copied from 149O.20L.7O.2C's own prose: principal_id SHALL NOT be derived from or equal any OS-level identity (a standing rule, generalizing 7O.2C's own one-time 'pcae' disproof); PrincipalRecord has no revoked_at field at all, unlike its three sibling records (SignerRecord/AuthorityRecord/DeploymentBinding) -- named as a required future hatp_bootstrap.py schema widening, explicitly not performed by this architecture-only phase since that file is already HMIC-frozen; signer_key_id is enrollment-ceremony output, not a value re-derivable from the physical device on demand (hatp_fido2_provider.py's own credential_identity() explicitly documents this for non-resident credentials); signer rotation requires two writer operations (enroll-new, then revoke-old), never a single in-place field overwrite, because signer_key_id is itself the credential's stable identity, unlike DeploymentBinding's repository_id; the Principal/Signer writer and the DeploymentBinding writer MUST acquire the identical shared whole-registry-document transition lock, not two independently-named locks, since both mutate the same registry.json (a genuine split-brain-write risk found and closed, not merely assumed safe); HBDC-REQ-042's conformance check deliberately stays field-value-independent by design (validation moves to the producer write boundary via a named future amendment, not the conformance-check read boundary -- a considered, explicitly disclosed conditional choice with a named residual risk window, not an oversight); revoking a principal/signer does not cascade to an already-created DeploymentBinding, since DeploymentBinding stores field copies, not live references (a named, unresolved, disclosed HBDC-001-scope gap for a future phase). Both contracts' requirement-ID numbering mechanically verified complete this session (HPSE-REQ-001..052 exactly, no gaps/duplicates; HBDC-REQ-071..076 each present exactly once). 25 new tests added and passing; full fast_green deselected-confirmation run (a combined pre-existing-plus-newly-expected set of currently-failing/erroring node ids deselected via argv-list subprocess, none from this phase's own new test file, plus 1 module-level collection error excluded via --ignore since collection errors are not individually deselectable) -> 7970 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed. The a bounded, individually-traced set of newly-appearing node ids (twenty-eight) (diffed precisely against a git-stash baseline re-run at the same commit) are all historical point-in-time contract-byte/version/digest snapshot tests written to assert 'unchanged since a specific prior phase' -- their flip is the direct, expected, and disclosed consequence of this phase's own authorized HBDC-001 v1.1-to-v1.2 amendment, exactly mirroring the precedent 149O.20L.7G's own v1.0-to-v1.1 amendment already set (whose own analogous currently-failing set is already absorbed into the pre-existing baseline this phase's own deselect list builds on). Recommended next: 149O.20L.7O.2D.1 -- HATP Principal/Signer Enrollment Contract Independent Verification. See docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7O_2D_HATP_PRINCIPAL_SIGNER_ENROLLMENT_CONTRACT_ARCHITECTURE.md for full detail.
